title: A trace that lasts longer: read, but no longer of one act
setup: Experiment 38b · experiment 38 with the trace fading by 3% a moment instead of 20% (strong for about twenty moments) · same runs and seeds · 5 lives each
question: Was experiment 38's trace never read because it was too short? If it lasts longer, does a word read it, and does it still tell who acted?

points: With words formed from it, the longer trace is read while strong after 8-11% of Olvasó's own answered acts (0.1% or fewer in experiment 38); without new words, barely more than the shuffled control.

It is read more often after the habit's acts (12-14%): a trace that lasts twenty moments is still on the hand when the next act comes, whoever does it. The hole that marked Olvasó's own acts fills in, and who acted can hardly be told from the reading (−0.01-0.01 without words, 0.13-0.19 with, against 0.28-0.58).
A lasting unread sense floods the life: 264-266 intentions a day (389-396 shuffled), the habit's share 3-6%, gaming's harm doubled; words formed from the trace bring it only part of the way back.
note: A trade-off, not a reversal of experiment 38: a trace short enough to belong to its act is too short to be read, and one long enough to be read no longer belongs to one act. Knowing one's own act from a felt trace would need a trace both lasting and tied to its act.
